english.title: Aid / abet the causing of serious injury by dangerous driving
english.standardoffencewording:

english.notes:
This offence was inserted into the Road Traffic Act 1988 by section 143 of, and Schedule 27 to the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 and comes into force on 03/12/2012.

(i) Section 1A(4) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that the offence shall only have effect relation to driving occurring after the subsection comes into force.
(ii) See section 2A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 for the meaning of dangerous driving.
(iii) Section 1A(2) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that "serious injury" means - in England and Wales, physical harm which amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences against the Person Act 1861, in Scotland, "severe physical injury".
(iv) See section 13A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 for disapplication of section 1A for authorised motoring events.
(v) Officers should ensure that they know the C.P.S. guidelines for this offence before preparing any charges. When investigating these offences consideration must be given to the advice offered in the charging standards.
(vi) In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 "12 months" is to be read as "6 months" (in England and Wales).

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

NB Until the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 12 months should be read as a reference to 6 months.
Obligatory endorsement 3 - 11 penalty points.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
